title: Get notebook
description: The full notebook view: title, markdown source, the notebook's variables (name, type, value; a SQL cell reads one as `{name}`, a Python cell as a global — change them with notebooks-set-variables), and every cell (the notebook's markdown prose included, as cell_type 'markdown') with its code, dataframe name, depends_on/dependents edges, and derived status — 'stale' means re-running the cell now would execute different code than its last completed run (the cell changed, an upstream changed, or, for a SQL cell that ran on ClickHouse, a variable it reads changed), so its displayed result is outdated. A changed variable value does not make a Python cell, or a SQL cell that reads a Python-created dataframe, stale: on those, 'done' means the code is current, not the values it ran with. Re-run them from the stale_cells list notebooks-set-variables returns, and re-run before trusting a result whose values may have changed since. Use this to read or orient in a notebook, find which cells need re-running after edits, and decide re-run order (walk stale cells in dependency order with notebooks-update-cell, omitting code). Each cell carries start and end: the character span of its source in markdown. A markdown cell's id is derived from its text, so edit it with notebooks-update-cell against the same read that returned it. Legacy rich-text notebooks return their raw document in content instead of markdown. When you do not have the notebook's short_id, find it with notebooks-list.
